doc.title: Keter Betts interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996

title: First recording with Bostic and the theater circuit
summary: A month after joining he recorded, with a bass-featured melody on 'Wrap Your Troubles in Dreams', and played the Apollo, Earle, Royal, Howard and Regal circuit.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What was your first recording experience?

With Bostic? A month after I’d joined him. And I got a featured thing. He had written this tune, I mean the arranger for “Wrap Your Troubles in Dreams” and the bass played the melody, so and the other side that he had was a hit so there was a lot of requests for that when we played the theaters. You know we were doing the circuit, the Apollo, and then there was the Earle in Philadelphia and the Royal in Baltimore and the Howard in Washington, and the Regal in Chicago. So when you made the circuit you made one, two, three, four, that’s a month there.
